source_title: 'He could be happier' - why is Estevao becoming Chelsea's forgotten man?
en_body:
Brazilian forward Estevao Willian, once the talk of the Premier League after scoring a late winner against Liverpool in October 2024, has become a peripheral figure at Chelsea under head coach Xabi Alonso. The 19-year-old, who joined from Palmeiras in summer 2024, has made just two starts across all competitions this season, accumulating only 172 minutes — 125 of which came in early Carabao Cup ties against Luton Town and Leeds United.

## Unused at Anfield Despite Attacking Absences

The clearest signal of Estevao's current standing came during Chelsea's Carabao Cup quarter-final defeat to Liverpool at Anfield on Wednesday. With Cole Palmer suspended and João Pedro injured, Chelsea's attacking options were depleted. Yet as the match progressed and Alonso made a triple substitution in the second half — introducing Emanuel Emegha, who had not previously featured for the club — Estevao was seen ending his warm-up and returning to the bench without entering the game.

## Zero Premier League Starts Under Alonso

Since Alonso's appointment in summer 2025, Estevao has not been named in the starting XI for any of Chelsea's eight Premier League matches. His only start in open play this season came in the 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds, where he was withdrawn at half-time with the team trailing 1-0. The Brazilian's lack of involvement persists even when first-choice attackers are unavailable.

## Alonso: "He Could Be Happier"

After the Liverpool defeat, Alonso acknowledged the forward's frustration while citing the physical demands of English football. "He could be happier. He wants to play. I'm sure Estevao will have his moment, it is my responsibility," the Spaniard said. "We know the game in England is really intense, and you need to be up for it. Estevao is in his second season. The season is going to be long."

Alonso also explained his selection logic for the Anfield match: "We started with Pedro [Neto], Morgan [Rogers] and Danny Welbeck, and the game had very intense moments. We knew it was going to be physical, and Malo [Gusto] had cramps, so we were a bit forced with substitutions."

## Neto's Revival Creates Positional Blockage

A primary factor in Estevao's limited role is the resurgence of Pedro Neto. The 26-year-old Portugal international, who appeared close to a move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli, has started seven of eight Premier League matches under Alonso and recently signed a new six-year contract. Neto operates primarily as a right-sided wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-2-1 system — a hybrid role requiring both attacking output and defensive discipline.

Former Reading midfielder Jobi McAnuff told Sky Sports: "He's a player who is a little bit of a victim of the system. Alonso tends to play Neto in that hybrid wing-back role, expecting him to get high up the pitch as well. Maybe he doesn't feel that suits Estevao, and I don't feel it does either."

Neto has scored four goals in 11 appearances this season, reinforcing Alonso's preference for a player with Premier League experience and greater defensive reliability in that position.

## Attacking Depth Further Crowds the Path

Even beyond the right flank, Chelsea's forward line is congested. Morgan Rogers, signed for £117 million from Aston Villa, has made a spectacular start alongside João Pedro and Cole Palmer. This trio has effectively secured the three most advanced attacking roles in Alonso's system, leaving few entry points for a player of Estevao's profile.

Former Crystal Palace forward Clinton Morrison expressed surprise at Estevao's continued omission against Liverpool: "How Estevao has not got on the pitch tonight, I do not know. He must be thinking, 'What do I have to do? We have injuries to two of the star players up front, and I'm still not getting on the pitch.'"

## Practical Implications and What Comes Next

For Chelsea, the situation presents both a challenge and an opportunity. The club invested significantly in a player widely regarded as one of Brazil's brightest prospects, yet the current tactical setup and squad depth leave no obvious pathway to regular minutes. Alonso's public backing — "the season is going to be long, and there will be moments for everyone" — suggests he views this as a developmental phase rather than a permanent exclusion.

For Estevao, the immediate priority is adapting to the physical and tactical demands Alonso has highlighted. His age (19) and the precedent of Neto's own career revival at the club offer reason for patience, but the January transfer window may bring loan speculation if the status quo persists.

For fantasy football and scouting observers, the key takeaway is clear: Estevao is not currently a viable selection asset, and his route to relevance depends on either a tactical shift, injuries to multiple senior attackers, or a loan move.

## What Is Confirmed vs. Unknown

**Confirmed:**
- Estevao has 2 starts, 172 total minutes this season (125 in Carabao Cup vs Luton/Leeds)
- Zero Premier League starts in 8 matches under Alonso
- Unused substitute vs Liverpool despite Palmer suspension and João Pedro injury
- Alonso publicly acknowledged Estevao's frustration and cited physical adaptation
- Neto has 7 PL starts, 4 goals in 11 games, new 6-year contract
- Rogers (£117m), Palmer, João Pedro are established first-choice attackers

**Unknown:**
- Whether Alonso will adjust system to accommodate Estevao
- If a January loan is under consideration by club or player
- Specific timeline for "moments" Alonso referenced
- Whether Estevao's training performances match his youth reputation
